title: Five-Out Press Release
description: Five offensive players spread the full court against three pressuring defenders, learning to pivot, pass away from traps and attack the open space.

content.objective: Beat full-court pressure by keeping spacing, passing away from traps and attacking open space instead of dribbling into the press.
content.setup: Five offensive players start on the baseline with the ball. Three defenders pressure in the first half of the court: one on the ball and two in the nearest passing lanes. Once the ball crosses half court, the group plays the possession out live to the far basket.
content.organization: Run in groups of eight: five on offense and three on defense, with the other groups waiting at the far baseline. Rotate after each possession so everyone plays both roles.
instructions: The inbounder passes to the ball handler at the free-throw line. The two wings spread to the sidelines and the fifth player fills the middle, near half court, to give safe passing options.
The ball handler pivots to protect the ball and looks first for the middle player, then the far side. Avoid dribbling toward the sideline, where a trap is easy to set.
If a trap comes, the nearest teammate steps toward the ball to give an outlet while the others space away, ready to catch and go.
Once the ball is past half court, play live 5v3 to a score or a stop; the defenders may fall back.
Count how many possessions in six get across half court cleanly. The goal is five.
coachingPoints: Pivot and see the floor before you dribble.
Pass away from pressure, not into it.
Sprint to open passing lanes; do not wait for the ball to come to you.
Stay spread: keep clear space between teammates so one defender cannot guard two players.
commonMistakes: Dribbling toward the sideline into a trap.
Cutters standing next to the ball handler instead of creating space.
Throwing long, high-risk passes across traffic.
content.safety: Defenders trap with hands up and no reaching or contact on the ball handler's body.
progressions: Add a fourth defender to deny the middle passing lane.
regressions: Start with only two defenders so the offense builds confidence and spacing habits.
variations: Allow the ball handler only two dribbles before the first pass.
